doc.title: Chico Hamilton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Bebop, band changes and the road
title: Meeting Hale Smith and the Dean Martin film
summary: He met Hale Smith through Jim Hall, Hale arranged for Gongs East and Eric Dolphy studied with him, and they later did films, including a shopping story from Mr. Rico.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: But that brings up a very important chapter, at least as far as musical history. Where did you meet Hale Smith and how? Was it in Cleveland?

No. I met Hale here in New York come to think about it, and he and Jim Hall knew each other because they were both from Cleveland and he came to a rehearsal we had and we hooked up and, you know, stayed friends ever since. And Hale did some charts for me, you know, but Jim Hall was the reason I met Hale. I think we were at Birdland at the time, you know. And he was here in New York.
Was that how he and Eric got hooked up or do you know how that relationship came?
He met Eric through me, through my group, and when Eric decided to stay in New York, he started studying with Hale, you know. So he went to school.
I’m holding a double reissue of Chico Hamilton Three Faces of Chico and Gongs East.
Gongs east.
And on Gongs East we have couple arrangements by Hale Smith.
By Hale?
Yeah.
Good.
So this is when I realized that that relationship goes back at least to 1959 if not earlier.
Oh, yeah.
1958, excuse me, 1958. So how did you engage him to do the arrangements? Did you ever hear of his work?
Very easily.
You heard his work or did you -­

Well Jim Hall, you know, told me what a fantastic musician he was. If Jim Hall said he was cool, he’s cool, you know, that type of thing. And I met him, I liked him, we liked each other, you know, and he said he’d like to do something for me, you know, for the group and he did and we went on to do a whole lot of things after that, you know. As a matter of fact we did a couple movies together.
We’ll return to that when we get to that stage of your career.
Yeah. It’s a funny thing, we went to California to do this film, right, and the film was with Dean Martin. I can’t think of -- oh, man, my memory’s gone. Anyway it was a Dean Martin film.
Was it the How to Succeed -- was that the one?
He played the part of a, you know -­
The ones I’ve got are Cool and Groovy, The Sweet Smell of Success. No, neither one of those?

Okay, Dean Martin -- Mr. Rico. Mr. Rico, right. So we go out there and we go shopping, right. Hale’s with me and I see a shirt that I like, right, silk shirt. So I think I paid about $100 or something for it. Hale flipped. I said, Hale let me -- you know, now you think that was extravagant, yeah, you know. I said, well hell, you smoke $25 cigars. So what’s the difference? You pay $25 for a cigar; I pay $100 for a shirt.
